quote: Sorry. You're super quiet. I can't hear you very well.
stewart_read: Rep names the audio problem directly instead of pretending to understand or guessing, which is the correct low-friction repair move and got a clear answer within one more exchange.
coaching_implication: No coaching needed here — this is a model of how to handle audio friction without burning the call.

quote: Gotcha. So the the tax incentive?
stewart_read: Customer's interest reason ('Colorado gave you 30,000 to put on solar') is a strong anchor, but the rep immediately reframes it into a generic tax-incentive label rather than reflecting the customer's own number back to build curiosity about what he specifically qualifies for.
alternative_hypothesis: Could be read as efficient clarification rather than a miss, since the rep needed to confirm what the customer meant.
coaching_implication: This became moot once the tax-credit disqualifier (retired, doesn't file taxes) surfaced seconds later and the call ended in an unrelated hard DQ. Minor note only — not worth heavy rep time, but the instinct to anchor on the customer's own words instead of relabeling them is a good general habit to name.

quote: I don't file taxes. I'm retired.
stewart_read: Customer discloses a fact that would gate the federal tax credit path (retired, no tax filing), and the rep simply acknowledges ('You're retired? Okay.') and moves to the next verify question without noting or flagging this for the closer.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged this irrelevant since the call was about to hit a separate, unrelated hard DQ (manufactured home) minutes later — in which case the omission carried no real cost on this call.
coaching_implication: Secondary/moot on this specific call since the manufactured-home DQ ended things anyway, but worth a passing mention: when a customer volunteers a tax-filing status, that's useful qualifying data even if this call didn't need it.

quote: Cool. Oh, yeah. I'm seeing the woodsheds. So the main one, the big ones would be the house and the garage then. Yeah.

quote: Let me check into one thing real quick, Tyler. I'm just gonna put you on hold. I'll be right back. Okay?

coaching_implication: This is the right procedural move — protects the customer's time and the closer's pipeline from a doomed booking. Reinforce this instinct as correct, not a delay to eliminate.

coaching_implication: Minor: consider a slightly warmer close ('I wish I had better news for you') even on hard DQs, since it costs nothing and leaves a better impression, though it wouldn't change the outcome here.
